  1652	  to a finite Galois extension \(L/k\): there are a finite-type proper group scheme \(J_L\)
  1653	  representing \(\mathrm{pic}^0(C_L)\), its universal class, and a semilinear action of
  1654	  \(\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)\) preserving that class and satisfying the cocycle condition.
  1655	  Every orbit of this action is contained in an affine open of \(J_L\).
  1656	\end{theorem}

  1658	  Because \(J_{k^s}\) is of finite presentation, it descends to a finite subextension
  1659	  \(L_0/k\).  The universal class descends after enlarging \(L_0\), by
  1660	  Theorem~\ref{thm:pic0DescentCompatibility}.  The natural transformation defined by the
  1661	  descended class becomes the given representation after extension to \(k^s\); faithful flat
  1662	  descent for both the Yoneda functor and the Picard sheaf shows that it is already an
  1663	  isomorphism over \(L_0\).  Properness, the group operations, and their finitely many axioms
  1664	  also descend after one further finite extension.  Enlarge \(L_0\) to a finite Galois
  1665	  extension \(L/k\).
  1666	
  1667	  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)\), both \(\sigma^*J_L\) and \(J_L\), equipped with
  1668	  their transported universal classes, represent the same functor.  Yoneda uniqueness gives
  1669	  a unique semilinear isomorphism between them.  The two composites associated to
  1670	  \(\sigma\tau\) carry the universal class to the same element, so uniqueness proves the
  1671	  cocycle equation.  A proper finite-type group scheme over a field is projective.  Given a
  1672	  finite Galois orbit, choose a closed specialization of each of its finitely many points.
  1673	  For a sufficiently high power of an ample line bundle, restriction of global sections to
  1674	  the resulting finite closed subscheme is surjective.  Lift the section that is \(1\) at
  1675	  every member of that subscheme.  Its nonvanishing locus contains the chosen closed
  1676	  specializations and therefore the original orbit; as the complement of an ample effective
  1677	  divisor, this locus is affine.  This proves the final certificate.
  1678	\end{proof}

  1680	\begin{lemma}[Stable affine neighbourhoods for a finite action]
  1681	  \label{lem:finiteGalois_stableAffineCover}
  1682	  \notready
  1683	  Let a finite group \(G\) act on a separated scheme \(X\).  If every \(G\)-orbit is contained
  1684	  in an affine open, then \(X\) has a \(G\)-stable affine open cover.
  1685	\end{lemma}
  1686	\begin{proof}
  1687	  Fix \(x\in X\) and choose an affine open \(V\) containing its whole orbit.  Every translate
  1688	  \(gV\) also contains that orbit.  Hence
  1689	  \(U_x=\bigcap_{g\in G}gV\) is a \(G\)-stable open containing \(x\).  A finite intersection
  1690	  of affine opens in a separated scheme is affine: the intersection of two is the inverse
  1691	  image of the affine \(V\times V'\) under the affine diagonal, and induction handles the
  1692	  finite intersection.  The opens \(U_x\), as \(x\) varies, form the required cover.
  1693	\end{proof}

  1700	  action satisfying the cocycle condition.  If every orbit lies in an affine open, then there

  1702	  \(X\times_kL\simeq X_L\) inducing the given action.

  1709	  same invariant construction to these overlaps descends both open immersions
  1710	  \(U_i\cap U_j\rightrightarrows U_i,U_j\); faithful flatness of \(L/k\) reflects the open
  1711	  immersions and their cocycle identities.  The affine schemes \(\Spec B_i\) therefore glue
  1712	  along the descended overlaps to a \(k\)-scheme \(X\).  The local isomorphisms
  1713	  \(L\otimes_kB_i\simeq A_i\) agree on overlaps and glue to
  1714	  \(X\times_kL\simeq X_L\).  Their defining invariant maps identify the canonical descent
  1715	  action with the prescribed semilinear action.
  1716	\end{proof}

  1725	  condition and the orbit-in-affine hypothesis.  Then there are a \(k\)-scheme \(X\) and a

  1733	  it.  Yoneda turns \(u\) into a natural map \(h_X\to F\).  After base change to \(L\) this is

  1594	\begin{theorem}[The rank-one representer supplies the descent package]
  1595	  \label{thm:pic0SepClosedDescentInput_exists}

  1605	  The commutative-group law on \(\mathrm{pic}^0(C)\) transfers uniquely across the
  1606	  representation to a group-scheme law on \(J_s\), and the image of the identity morphism is
  1607	  its universal class.  The translated rank-one charts show that \(J_s\) is locally of finite
  1608	  type.  Its identity point is closed because it is a rational point of a scheme locally of
  1609	  finite type over a field.  The diagonal is the inverse image of that point under the
  1610	  difference morphism \(J_s\times J_s\to J_s\), so the group scheme is separated.
  1611	
  1612	  Choose a point of \(C\) over the separably closed base and use its \(g(C)\)-fold divisor to
  1613	  translate the degree-\(g(C)\) Abel map to \(\mathrm{pic}^0(C)\).  After any algebraically
  1614	  closed extension, Riemann--Roch gives a section of every degree-\(g(C)\) line bundle, so this
  1615	  translated Abel map \(D_g\to J_s\) is surjective.  It is proper because \(D_g\) is projective
  1616	  and \(J_s\) is separated.  A surjective image of the quasi-compact scheme \(D_g\) makes
  1617	  \(J_s\) quasi-compact; combined with local finite type, this gives finite type.  Properness
  1618	  descends through the surjective proper map: after every base change, the image in the base
  1619	  of a closed subset of \(J_s\) is the image of its closed inverse image in \(D_g\), hence is
  1620	  closed.  Finally, the geometric fibres of \(D_g\) are irreducible by
  1621	  Theorem~\ref{thm:genusDivisorSource_geometry}, and their surjective images are irreducible.
  1622	  These are exactly the certificates required by the package.

  1625	\begin{theorem}[Limit and faithfully flat compatibility of \(\mathrm{pic}^0\)]
  1626	  \label{thm:pic0DescentCompatibility}
  1627	  \uses{def:pic0Functor}
  1628	  \notready

  1630	  satisfies effective descent along faithfully flat field extensions, compatibly with its
  1631	  universal classes.

  1633	\begin{proof}
  1634	  An invertible sheaf is given on a finite affine cover by finitely many finitely presented
  1635	  rank-one modules, transition isomorphisms, and finitely many cocycle equations.  All this
  1636	  data, as well as an isomorphism between two such data, descends to a finite stage of a
  1637	  filtered union.  The degree-zero condition is preserved and reflected after field extension
  1638	  because degree is invariant under scalar extension.  This proves filtered compatibility.
  1639	  Faithfully flat descent for finitely presented modules descends the local line bundles and
  1640	  their transition maps, while the cocycle equation gives effectivity and uniqueness.  Passing
  1641	  to the quotient by line bundles from the base and then to the etale sheafification preserves
  1642	  this descent statement, since both equivalence and effectivity may be checked after a common
  1643	  faithfully flat refinement.
  1644	\end{proof}

---
name: leansearch
description: Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
---

**Search before you prove.** Most facts you need already exist in mathlib or the
workspace. Searching is far cheaper than reproving. Use the local index first
(unlimited, instant), then the LSP search tools for broader semantic/type search.

## Local first: `horizon search`

An offline declaration search over `external_libraries` (mathlib by default) plus
the workspace's own projects. No GPU, API key, or network. Three modes share one
cached index:

- Natural language — what a lemma says:
  `horizon search "continuous function on a compact set attains its maximum"`
- `--name` — find a declaration by partial name:
  `horizon search --name isCompact.image`
- `--type` — find by shape of the statement; `?a`/`?b`/`_` are wildcards:
  `horizon search --type "Continuous ?f -> IsCompact ?s -> IsCompact (?f '' ?s)"`

Useful flags: `-n K`, `--lib NAME`, `--json`, `--reindex`. If results look thin,
run the project build so sources are current, then `horizon search --reindex`.

## Lean LSP MCP search tools

The `lean-lsp` MCP server (configured in `.mcp.json`) exposes a full search
arsenal. Rate limits are **per-tool** (separate pools), not a shared budget.

| Tool | Use it for | Limit |
|------|-----------|-------|
| `lean_local_search` | exact/partial declaration name; workspace + mathlib | unlimited |
| `lean_leansearch` | **semantic search by mathematical meaning** (PKU LeanSearch) | 10 / 30s |
| `lean_loogle` | search by **type shape** when you know the signature, not the name | remote; unlimited in `--loogle-local` |
| `lean_state_search` | lemmas that apply to a specific **proof state** (goal at a line) | 3 / 30s |
| `lean_hammer_premise` | **premise names** to feed `simp only [...]` / `aesop` / `grind` | 3 / 30s |
| `lean_leanfinder` | semantic fallback — only when `lean_leansearch` fails | 10 / 30s |

### Priority / escalation order

1. `lean_local_search("name")` — always first; unlimited, instant, deterministic.
2. `lean_leansearch("describe the math.")` — primary semantic search (see below).
3. `lean_loogle("?a -> ?b")` — simple type patterns only.
4. `lean_state_search(file, line, col)` — goal-conditioned lookup when stuck.
5. `lean_hammer_premise(file, line, col)` — premises for `simp`/`aesop`/`grind`.
6. `lean_leanfinder("description")` — last-resort semantic fallback.

### `lean_leansearch` — the PKU semantic tool (use it well)

LeanSearch (leansearch.net, from the PKU team) augments each mathlib theorem into
an informal description and matches your query against those embeddings —
returning the **nearest neighbours**, not just exact hits. That is its strength:
a theorem 90% of what you need is often enough; prove the small gap yourself.

- **Describe the mathematical content, not the name.** Query must end with `.`/`?`.
  - Good: `lean_leansearch("The image of a compact set under a continuous map is compact.")`
  - Good (mixed): `lean_leansearch("natural numbers. from: n < m, to: n + 1 < m + 1")`
  - Weak: `lean_leansearch("add_comm")` → use `lean_local_search` instead.
  - Weak: `lean_leansearch("∀ (a b : ℕ), a + b = b + a")` → use `lean_loogle` instead.
- **Trust a negative result.** If a precise, mathematically accurate description
  returns nothing relevant, the theorem likely isn't in mathlib — stop rephrasing
  and prove it (or find another route) rather than searching endlessly.

### `lean_loogle` — type-shape search

Searches by *type structure*, not names. Syntax: `?a`/`?b` type vars, `_`
wildcards, `->`/`→` arrows, `|- pattern` by conclusion.
- Good: `lean_loogle("(?a -> ?b) -> List ?a -> List ?b")` → `List.map`
- Anti-pattern: nested `Submodule`/`LinearMap`/`Finsupp`, 3+ typeclass
  constraints, or guessy implicit structure — use `lean_leansearch` for those.

## Discipline

- Treat every hit as a **candidate**: read the signature/source and confirm with
  the Lean checker (see the `lean-check` skill) before depending on it.
- Try multiple phrasings — project name, mathematical concept, conclusion/type.
- Local (`horizon search` / `lean_local_search`) is optimized for the checked-out
  sources here; the LSP tools reach broader mathlib precedent. Use both.

     8	/-!
     9	# Assembly from a rank-one divisor-fibre pullback
    10	
    11	This file isolates the last presheaf step in the arbitrary-scheme rank-one fibre construction.
    12	Its input ties an open `W` to the displayed family, supplies native presentations on every
    13	affine pullback, and supplies the canonical evaluation-divisor classifier.  The geometric input
    14	to the assembly theorem is the genuine pullback square of that evaluation divisor along Abel.
    15	The universal property of this stronger square produces, rather than assumes, the factorisation
    16	field of `PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented`.
    17	
    18	The global construction of the canonical classifier and its represented pullbacks remains an
    19	upstream obligation.  The endpoint here keeps that obligation in its geometric `IsPullback`
    20	form and feeds the resulting arbitrary-scheme fibres immediately to
    21	`picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_fibrePresented`.
    22	
    23	Thus this module is a conditional assembly interface, not the missing global producer: no
    24	declaration below constructs the evaluator, the open family, or its pullback theorem.
    25	-/
    26	
    27	set_option autoImplicit false
    28	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    29	
    30	universe u
    31	
    32	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    33	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    34	
    35	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    36	
    37	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    38	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

    42	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

    48	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))

    52	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor
    53	
    54	/-- The divisor families whose Abel class has a rank-one presentation, extended to the big site. -/
    55	abbrev rankOneDivisorLocus : Schemeᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
    56	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))
    57	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor
    58	
    59	/-- The restricted represented Abel map on the big site. -/
    60	def rankOneAbelSigma :
    61	    rankOneDivisorLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) ⟶
    62	      rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) :=
    63	  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (rankOneAbelRepresented pi)
    64	
    65	/-- The ambient class of a divisor already known to lie in the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
    66	def rankOneDivisorToAmbient :
    67	    rankOneDivisorLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) ⟶ rankOneAmbient (C := C) :=
    68	  rankOneAbelSigma pi ≫ picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi
    69	
    70	/-! ## The explicit geometric input -/
    71	
    72	/-- The single canonical evaluation-divisor classifier used by every represented fibre.
    73	
    74	Keeping this datum outside `PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput` prevents the classifier from
    75	varying with the test scheme or displayed family. -/
    76	structure PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData where
    77	  divisor : rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) ⟶
    78	    rankOneDivisorLocus (C := C) (pi := pi)
    79	  divisor_abel : divisor ≫ rankOneAbelSigma pi = 𝟙 _
    80	
    81	namespace PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData
    82	
    83	/-- Applying restricted Abel to the canonical evaluation divisor recovers its rank-one class. -/
    84	lemma divisor_abel_app (E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi)
    85	    (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : (rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi)).obj (op S)) :
    86	    (rankOneAbelSigma pi).app (op S) (E.divisor.app (op S) v) = v := by
    87	  exact congrArg (fun q => q.app (op S) v) E.divisor_abel

    91	    E.divisor ≫ rankOneDivisorToAmbient pi = picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi := by
    92	  rw [rankOneDivisorToAmbient, ← Category.assoc, E.divisor_abel, Category.id_comp]

    95	preimage is the canonical evaluation divisor of its Abel class. -/
    96	def AbelInverse (E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi) : Prop :=
    97	  rankOneAbelSigma pi ≫ E.divisor = 𝟙 _
    98

   100	rank-one family isomorphism. -/
   101	def evaluationIso (E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi) (h : E.AbelInverse) :
   102	    rankOneDivisorLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) ≅ rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) where
   103	  hom := rankOneAbelSigma pi
   104	  inv := E.divisor
   105	  hom_inv_id := h
   106	  inv_hom_id := E.divisor_abel
   107	
   108	end PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData
   109	
   110	/--
   111	The explicit data needed to assemble one arbitrary-scheme rank-one fibre.
